idea.value: A product that turns one typed sentence into a finished launch film sells itself by being exactly such a film: the promise is typed on screen in the first two seconds, then the product's own toolbox of moves (typed lines, iris wipes, a 3D phone, an orbit of thumbnails) is performed in front of the viewer, and the prompt-to-result demo sits in the middle as proof.
evidence: speech-text.json screenText 0.30-1.37 s: the promise line builds word by word
speech-text.json screenText 10.27-13.27 s: the prompt typed in the product asks for a 30-second launch film

audience.value: Founders and indie app makers who need a launch film and would otherwise open professional editing suites or hire a motion designer.

value.device: The whole promise as one short line built word by word on a white ground, a new word every 10 frames, each word arriving pale lilac, turning raspberry, then teal, and settling to ink about 5 frames later, inside four corner dots that spread with the line like a selection box; at 1.80-1.97 s the two halves of the line drift apart, then a hard cut to a cinematic plate.
value.description: The first frame already holds a word; the line answers 'what is this' in 1.4 s with no logo. The selection-box dots read as an editor's frame, so the viewer is primed for 'something is being made'. The split of the line at 1.8 s opens a gap that the hard cut to a photographic plate fills.

value.retentionDevice: An unfinished sentence: each word is a small event every 0.33 s
value.content: One-line promise typed word by word in a corner-dot frame; the line splits into its two phrases before the cut.

value.purpose: Context: the tools people use today, then the product singled out among them
value.retentionDevice: A black card collapsing into a selection underline; a punch-in; the selection travelling along a dock
value.content: Coastal plate with a bridge; a black card shrinks into the underline of a floating icon dock; punch-in with background defocus; the dock slides left until the product's mark is the last icon and the others blur.

value.retentionDevice: Three different reveals in 3.9 s: iris to dark, word on an arc, mark-plus-wordmark lockup
value.content: A dark disc sweeps over everything except the mark; the name types under it in small capitals; hard cut to white with 'Introducing' rising on an arc; hard cut to the mark, the wordmark slides out from behind it; the mark detaches and rises to the top.

value.purpose: Proof: the product in use, from prompt to generation
value.retentionDevice: The caret and the progress rows: something is always being written
value.content: A circle opens around the mark into the product's prompt screen on a pastel ground; the prompt types; punch-in on the field; a cursor goes to send; hard cut to the chat view; a six-step checklist ticks off.

value.retentionDevice: Depth: a 3D device, then a ring of thumbnails orbiting the line
value.content: The generated app shown in a tilted 3D phone; then a ring of about 30 photo thumbnails orbits a centred line about range, and flies outward past the frame.

value.retentionDevice: Second line typed with a visible caret under a held headline; four coloured chips drift
value.content: Large headline about speed with four small feature chips floating around it; a grey second line typed under it.

value.retentionDevice: The headline rolls away into a spinning mark that settles; the name types in tinted letters
value.content: Large rotated mark settles small and square; the wordmark types beside it; a dark button and the address fade up; still hold with silence for the last 0.83 s.

payoff.value: The headline claims a polished film in minutes; the viewer has just watched 30 s of the very moves the checklist promised, so the claim lands as already demonstrated.
evidence: speech-text.json screenText 21.13-23.02 s headline and second line

callToAction.value: Free-start button and web address under the centred mark-plus-wordmark lockup, held still for 2.2 s, the last 0.83 s in silence.

whyItWorks: The medium is the proof: every move after the demo is a move the product claims to make, so no testimonial is needed.
One persistent object, the mark, is carried through five boundaries (5.7, 7.83, 9.43 s and back at 24.53 s); the eye always knows where to look after a change.
Text is always being written: words arrive tinted and settle to ink, a caret types, checklist rows append. Reading rhythm replaces voiceover.
Ground alternates white, photographic, dark, white, pastel, white: each section is recognisable by its ground, and the only dark shot is the name reveal.
The demo shows the actual interaction (type, click, wait), not a summary of it, at a scale a viewer can read thanks to the punch-in.
